title: Construct color chorus and proportional radius lattice
creator: Asha Patel
description: Scope: Create a coherent token set that (1) introduces a perceptually-consistent color 'chorus' for brand, accents, and semantic states; (2) defines a proportional radius lattice that scales with component density; (3) revises shadow/elevation steps for compact and spacious modes; and (4) updates the typographic scale delta to sit ergonomically with the new token set. Goals: reduce token sprawl, make visual deltas predictable across components, guarantee WCAG AA contrast for primary/secondary actions at typical densities, and provide clear migration rules for buttons, tables and charts. Deliverables: token JSON with named tokens and aliases, Figma styles, migration guide for engineers, unit tests for contrast and visual regression, PRs for component library updates, and rollout checklist for console and docs.
acceptance_criteria: Token JSON published in /design/tokens/v2 with version tag
Figma file updated with new color styles and radius tokens
Automated contrast checks pass for primary/secondary button variants at 14px and 16px sizes
Table row rhythm preserved at compact and default densities with new radius lattice
Chart series colors mapped to new palette with no more than 3 indistinguishable color pairs for color-blind palettes
Release notes and migration guide merged to docs before release
comments: 2026-03-02 — Kickoff: scoped down to avoid full palette rewrite; focus on 3 semantic ramps + neutral family + accent harmonizer.
2026-03-04 — Design review: PM asked to preserve existing CTA hue for recognition; solution is token aliasing so legacy token points to new palette hue for two releases.
2026-03-06 — Engineering sync: agreed to ship token JSON and a small helpers library (ts) for runtime alias resolution to allow staged cutover.
2026-03-08 — Accessibility audit: initial palette failed AA on 12/14 button text; increased contrast by reducing background luminance by 6 points; rechecked against dynamic text sizes.
2026-03-11 — Prototype: buttons/tables updated in the component playground; visual diffs acceptable for >90% of cases; 3 chart color mappings flagged for ambiguity under deuteranopia simulator.
2026-03-12 — Decision: add a purpose-driven accent (accent-cta, accent-info) and a high-contrast alias layer; created ENG subtasks for chart color remapping.
migration_notes: Phased migration: 1) Publish v2 tokens with aliases mapping to v1 names, 2) Ship component updates reading tokens/v2, 3) Enable opt-in flag for runtime alias resolution, 4) Flip default after 2 weeks of rollout with monitoring for visual regressions. Provide a codemod for CSS/SCSS references and a short linter rule to detect legacy token usage.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Accessibility vs visual subtlety: higher contrast reduces subtlety in neutral surfaces; chosen compromise leans to accessibility for any body/label text.
- Back-compat: aliasing increases complexity but avoids a big-bang visual change.
- Chart semantics: reducing palette saturation for better contrast reduces maximum color distinctiveness; resolved by reserving three saturated accents for critical series and a secondary harmonized ramp for additional series.
implementation_plan: 1) Publish token schema and helpers (TS) -> 2) Design approves Figma styles -> 3) ENG implements tokens in component library (buttons, table rows, chart mappings) -> 4) Run visual regression and accessibility pipelines -> 5) Docs + release notes -> 6) Canary release -> 7) Full rollout and monitor.
release_notes: Introduces v2 design tokens: refined neutral ramps, accessible CTA aliasing, proportional radius lattice (compact/default), and a new 5-step elevation stack tuned for compact surfaces. Migration aliases included for backward compatibility.
rollout_plan: Canary in staging for 72 hours, visually compare top-20 dashboards and onboarding flows, collect SLO/UX feedback, then 7-day gradual rollout. Emergency rollback via alias toggle in runtime helpers if regressions detected.

Visual diff < 2% of key flows (login, create-workflow, run-eval)

notes_for_engineering: Use the helpers package to resolve aliases at build/runtime; keep token keys stable (token.primary, token.accent.cta) and avoid exposing raw hex color literals in components. Create a feature flag to flip between v1 and v2 palettes during rollout.
